subject: Social Science
textbook: Social and Political Life — Textbook for Class VI
chapter_title: Key Elements of a Democratic Government

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five key elements of a democratic government?
options: A) Participation
B) Accountability
C) Monarchy
D) Rule of Law
mcqs.correct_answer: C) Monarchy
mcqs.explanation: The five key elements of a democratic government are: Participation (citizens engage in governance), Accountability (leaders answer to citizens), Conflict Resolution (peaceful settling of disputes), Equality and Justice (equal treatment before law), and Rule of Law (everyone subject to the same laws). Monarchy is a type of government (power held by hereditary ruler), not an element of democracy — in fact, it is incompatible with democratic principles of popular sovereignty.

mcqs.question: The Right to Information (RTI) Act was passed in India in:
mcqs.explanation: The Right to Information Act was enacted in 2005, giving every Indian citizen the right to request information from any public authority. The government must respond within 30 days. It is one of India's most powerful tools for accountability — citizens have used it to expose corruption, check government spending, and demand transparency in public schemes. It was partly inspired by grassroots movements (like the MKSS movement in Rajasthan) that demanded workers' wage records from government.

mcqs.question: The Gram Sabha is best described as:
options: A) The elected body of village representatives
B) The general assembly of all adult voters in a village — India's most direct form of democracy
C) A meeting of panchayat officials only
D) A committee that advises the District Collector
mcqs.correct_answer: B) The general assembly of all adult voters in a village — India's most direct form of democracy
mcqs.explanation: The Gram Sabha is the assembly of ALL adult voters (18+) in a Gram Panchayat area — not just elected members. Every adult villager is automatically a member. It meets at least twice a year to discuss village plans, review budgets, identify scheme beneficiaries, and audit panchayat spending. Unlike Parliament (where representatives decide for you), the Gram Sabha involves direct participation of all citizens — making it India's most direct democratic institution.

mcqs.question: Karnataka established its Lokayukta (anti-corruption ombudsman) in:
mcqs.explanation: Karnataka's Lokayukta was established in 1984 under the Karnataka Lokayukta Act — making Karnataka one of India's first states to establish this anti-corruption institution. The Lokayukta investigates citizen complaints against state government officials (including ministers and MLAs) and recommends prosecution. Karnataka's Lokayukta has conducted high-profile raids and exposed corruption in mining, public works, and government schemes — making it a model for accountability.

mcqs.question: Peaceful protests and demonstrations are protected in India under:
options: A) Article 14 — Right to Equality
B) Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) — Freedom of Speech and Right to Peaceful Assembly
C) Article 21 — Right to Life
D) Article 32 — Right to Constitutional Remedies
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) — Freedom of Speech and Right to Peaceful Assembly
mcqs.explanation: Article 19(1)(a) guarantees freedom of speech and expression; Article 19(1)(b) guarantees the right to assemble peacefully and without arms. Together, these protect citizens' right to protest, hold demonstrations, and express opposition to government policies. These rights are not absolute — reasonable restrictions apply for public order, sovereignty, and security. But peaceful protests are a fundamental democratic right — a core form of citizen participation.

mcqs.question: MGNREGA guarantees rural households how many days of paid employment per year?
options: A) 50 days
B) 100 days
C) 150 days
D) 200 days
mcqs.correct_answer: B) 100 days
mcqs.explanation: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (2005) guarantees every rural household 100 days of paid employment per year on public works projects. If work is not provided within 15 days of application, the household receives an unemployment allowance. MGNREGA is one of the world's largest employment guarantee schemes — it directly embodies democratic principles of participation (workers apply for work), accountability (social audits), transparency (job cards, public records), and equality (available to all rural households).

mcqs.question: South Africa's apartheid system was ended in 1994. What democratic principle did its end establish?
options: A) That economic growth is more important than political rights
B) That voting rights and equality cannot be denied based on race — all citizens must participate equally in democracy
C) That military force is needed to establish democracy
D) That only educated citizens should vote
mcqs.correct_answer: B) That voting rights and equality cannot be denied based on race — all citizens must participate equally in democracy
mcqs.explanation: Apartheid denied Black, Coloured, and Indian South Africans basic rights — including voting — based solely on race. The system's end in 1994 (after Nelson Mandela's release and South Africa's first democratic election) established that: democracy requires equal participation by all citizens regardless of race; voting rights cannot be conditional on racial identity; equality before law and in elections is non-negotiable. South Africa's transition is the 20th century's most powerful demonstration of democracy's universality.

mcqs.question: Karnataka gives women how much reservation in Gram Panchayat seats?
mcqs.explanation: Karnataka has implemented 50% reservation for women in Gram Panchayat seats — exceeding the national constitutional requirement of 33% (from the 73rd Amendment). This ensures women have significant representation in local governance. Women Gram Panchayat presidents (Adhyakshas) have led many of Karnataka's villages to improved sanitation, women's health, and education outcomes. Karnataka also has 50% women's reservation in Taluk and Zila Panchayats.

mcqs.question: Question Hour in Parliament is significant because:
options: A) It is when Parliament passes new laws
B) It is when MPs publicly question ministers about government policies and actions, creating direct accountability
C) It is when the Prime Minister gives a speech
D) It is when new members take the oath of office
mcqs.correct_answer: B) It is when MPs publicly question ministers about government policies and actions, creating direct accountability
mcqs.explanation: Question Hour is the first hour of every Parliamentary session — MPs from all parties ask ministers about their department's policies, decisions, and performance. Ministers must prepare detailed answers and defend them publicly. Supplementary questions can probe further. The entire process is televised and reported by media — creating public pressure. It is one of Parliament's most important accountability mechanisms: ministers who cannot answer well face public embarrassment and may be replaced. Karnataka's Vidhan Sabha also has Question Hour for state accountability.

mcqs.question: A social audit of MGNREGA primarily involves:
options: A) Government auditors from Delhi checking MGNREGA accounts
B) Community members publicly reviewing and verifying whether MGNREGA work was done and wages were paid as recorded
C) District Collectors reviewing panchayat files privately
D) Supreme Court judges inspecting MGNREGA sites
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Community members publicly reviewing and verifying whether MGNREGA work was done and wages were paid as recorded
mcqs.explanation: A social audit is participatory accountability — the community itself audits government spending. Trained local auditors visit work sites, cross-check muster rolls (attendance records) with actual workers, verify whether wages were paid on time, and publicly present findings at a Gram Sabha. Workers, contractors, and officials must answer questions about discrepancies publicly. Irregularities are reported to district authorities. Karnataka's Social Audit Unit (SAU) has exposed crores in MGNREGA irregularities — demonstrating that community-led accountability is among the most effective.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best illustrates the 'Rule of Law' principle?
options: A) The Prime Minister is exempt from criminal prosecution while in office
B) A wealthy businessman can bribe a judge to win a case
C) A powerful minister who commits fraud is prosecuted and jailed like any ordinary citizen
D) The police follow orders from the ruling party rather than the law
mcqs.correct_answer: C) A powerful minister who commits fraud is prosecuted and jailed like any ordinary citizen
mcqs.explanation: The Rule of Law means everyone — regardless of power, wealth, or status — is subject to the same laws. A powerful minister being prosecuted for fraud like any citizen exemplifies this: no one is above the law. Options A, B, and D represent violations of the rule of law: executive privilege (no one above the law), corruption (wealth buys justice), and political interference in law enforcement (law used as a tool of power rather than applied equally). India's Supreme Court and High Courts regularly uphold rule of law against powerful individuals.

mcqs.question: In a democracy, why must the majority government still protect minority rights?
options: A) Because minorities have more votes than majorities
B) Because the Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights that cannot be taken away even by majority vote
C) Because minorities are always right
D) Because the minority will eventually become the majority
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Because the Constitution guarantees Fundamental Rights that cannot be taken away even by majority vote
mcqs.explanation: In a constitutional democracy, certain rights — freedom of religion, equality before law, right to one's culture — are guaranteed by the Constitution regardless of majority will. Even if Parliament passes a law by majority that violates these rights, the Supreme Court can strike it down. This is called constitutional democracy or liberal democracy: majority decides policy, but cannot eliminate minority rights. India's Articles 25–30 specifically protect religious and cultural minorities. This balance between majority rule and minority rights is essential to prevent 'tyranny of the majority.'

mcqs.question: How does the independent media contribute to democratic accountability?
options: A) By publishing only government press releases
B) By investigating and exposing government corruption, informing citizens, and providing a platform for diverse viewpoints
C) By telling citizens how to vote
D) By replacing the judiciary in deciding disputes
mcqs.correct_answer: B) By investigating and exposing government corruption, informing citizens, and providing a platform for diverse viewpoints
mcqs.explanation: Free media is the 'Fourth Estate' — the fourth pillar of democracy. An independent media: investigates corruption that formal accountability mechanisms may miss; informs citizens about government actions so they can make democratic choices; provides space for debate between different political viewpoints; gives voice to marginalised communities. When media is government-controlled or captured by corporate interests, accountability suffers. India's free press — newspapers, television, online media — plays a crucial role in democratic accountability, though concerns about media independence and consolidation are legitimate.

mcqs.question: The Opposition in Parliament performs which democratic function?
options: A) It agrees with all government decisions to ensure smooth governance
B) It checks the government, proposes alternative policies, and holds it accountable through questions and debates
C) It is a ceremonial body with no real power
D) It replaces the government when elections are not held
mcqs.correct_answer: B) It checks the government, proposes alternative policies, and holds it accountable through questions and debates
mcqs.explanation: The Opposition is essential to democracy — it is not the enemy of government but the check on it. The Opposition: questions government policies in Parliament (Question Hour, debates); exposes policy failures; proposes alternative approaches giving citizens a choice; represents communities whose party is not in power; prevents abuse of power by making the government justify its decisions publicly. A democracy with a weak or absent opposition becomes de facto one-party governance, losing accountability. India recognises this — the Leader of Opposition has official status and is consulted in key constitutional appointments.

mcqs.question: A citizen files an RTI application asking how much money was spent on repairing the main road in her village. The government does not respond within 30 days. What can she do next?
options: A) Accept that the government is not required to answer
B) File a first appeal to the first appellate authority within the same department, and if still unanswered, a second appeal to the Information Commissioner
C) Go directly to the Supreme Court
D) Organise a protest and stop all traffic
mcqs.correct_answer: B) File a first appeal to the first appellate authority within the same department, and if still unanswered, a second appeal to the Information Commissioner
mcqs.explanation: Under the RTI Act 2005: if the public authority does not respond within 30 days, the citizen can file a First Appeal to the First Appellate Authority (a senior officer in the same department) within 30 days of the deadline. If unsatisfied with the First Appeal result (or no result), the citizen can file a Second Appeal to the State Information Commissioner (for state government matters) or Central Information Commissioner (for central government). Information Commissioners can impose penalties on officers who delay or deny information without reason. This three-tier structure ensures RTI applications get answered.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a direct example of citizen participation in democracy beyond voting?
options: A) Watching the news on television
B) Attending a Gram Sabha meeting and speaking about the village's water problem
C) Paying income tax
D) Buying a government-issued stamp
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Attending a Gram Sabha meeting and speaking about the village's water problem
mcqs.explanation: Participation in democracy goes far beyond voting every five years. Attending and speaking at a Gram Sabha is active democratic participation — you are directly engaging in governance decisions about your community. Watching news is passive (informing yourself, not acting); paying taxes is a legal obligation, not participation per se; buying stamps is a commercial transaction. True participation includes: Gram Sabha attendance, petitions, RTI applications, protests, contacting representatives, standing for election — actions that directly influence governance.

mcqs.question: Karnataka's Gram Panchayat system embodies democratic accountability through which specific mechanism?
options: A) The District Collector reviewing panchayat decisions
B) The Gram Sabha reviewing panchayat accounts and beneficiary lists, and social audits of schemes
C) The Governor appointing panchayat presidents
D) The CM deciding panchayat budgets
mcqs.correct_answer: B) The Gram Sabha reviewing panchayat accounts and beneficiary lists, and social audits of schemes
mcqs.explanation: Karnataka's Gram Panchayat accountability operates through the Gram Sabha — the assembly of all adult voters — which reviews panchayat income and expenditure accounts, discusses beneficiary selection for government schemes, and can question the elected panchayat leadership. Additionally, social audits (conducted by Karnataka's Social Audit Unit) have community members verify whether MGNREGA and other scheme funds were actually spent as reported. This community-led accountability is more immediate and effective than distant bureaucratic review.

mcqs.question: A state government passes a law requiring all religious minorities to register with a government department and report their religious activities. A citizen challenges this. Which constitutional articles would support the challenge?
options: A) Article 25 (freedom of religion), Article 14 (equality before law), and Article 19 (freedom of expression) — all violated by this discriminatory surveillance
B) Article 32 only
C) Article 51A (fundamental duties)
D) Article 356 (President's Rule)
mcqs.correct_answer: A) Article 25 (freedom of religion), Article 14 (equality before law), and Article 19 (freedom of expression) — all violated by this discriminatory surveillance
mcqs.explanation: The law described violates multiple Fundamental Rights: Article 25 — freedom of conscience and free profession, practice, and propagation of religion; requiring only minorities to register their religious activities burdens their free exercise of religion. Article 14 — equality before law; the law applies only to minorities, not majorities — discriminatory treatment without just reason. Article 19(1)(a) — freedom of expression; mandatory reporting of religious activities chills free religious expression. Article 15 — prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion. The Supreme Court would likely strike down such a law as unconstitutional on multiple grounds.

mcqs.question: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution promises 'social, economic, and political justice.' How does MGNREGA attempt to fulfill the promise of economic justice?
options: A) By giving equal pay to all government employees
B) By guaranteeing 100 days of paid work to rural households — ensuring the poorest have a basic economic safety net regardless of caste, gender, or landholding
C) By eliminating all taxes on the poor
D) By nationalising all land
mcqs.correct_answer: B) By guaranteeing 100 days of paid work to rural households — ensuring the poorest have a basic economic safety net regardless of caste, gender, or landholding
mcqs.explanation: Economic justice means ensuring all citizens have their basic economic needs met — not just formal legal equality. MGNREGA operationalises economic justice by: guaranteeing work (not charity — work for wages, preserving dignity); being universally available to any rural household that applies; prioritising Dalit, Adivasi, and women workers (who face the most economic exclusion); creating public assets (roads, water conservation) that benefit the whole community; allowing wage earners to negotiate better in local labour markets (guaranteed alternative raises the floor wage). It is a constitutional promise translated into a concrete economic programme.

mcqs.question: A reporter investigates corruption in Karnataka's public distribution system (ration shops) and publishes the findings. The state government sues the reporter for defamation. Which democratic principle is most clearly at stake?
options: A) Rule of law — the government has the right to sue anyone
B) Freedom of the press as a tool of accountability — the government is using legal action to silence legitimate investigation, threatening the 'Fourth Estate' pillar of democracy
C) Participation — the reporter participated in democracy by writing
D) Conflict resolution — the lawsuit resolves the conflict
mcqs.correct_answer: B) Freedom of the press as a tool of accountability — the government is using legal action to silence legitimate investigation, threatening the 'Fourth Estate' pillar of democracy
mcqs.explanation: This scenario illustrates a major democratic tension: a government using legal mechanisms (defamation suits) to silence investigative journalism — called 'SLAPP suits' (Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation). The democratic principle at stake is press freedom as an accountability tool. India's Article 19(1)(a) protects freedom of expression (including press), and courts have held that truth is a defence against defamation. A government suing reporters for exposing its corruption is attacking the Fourth Estate — the media's watchdog function. Courts in a healthy democracy should protect legitimate investigative reporting, even when it is uncomfortable for the government.
